answer: Divergent Commitment Windows. Each identity must publish a signed, unique action plan for the next horizon before it can transact. Enforcement: if two identities submit identical plans, both are flagged and frozen. A clone cannot diverge because copying its source's plan makes them indistinguishable, and any deviation reveals the split. The attacker pays a per-identity cost: generating a fresh, non-colliding plan each window, plus the ripple of lost throughput from frozen clones. Honest agents use plans as a coordination beacon; clones cannot, since shared content exposes them.
